column1: # Every topic of the stack, in one place. create-topics.sh reads this file.
# Columns, separated by tabs:
#   name          the topic name
#   partitions    how many pieces the topic is split into; more partitions
#                 means more consumers can read it at the same time
#   key           what the producer uses as the message key, so that all
#                 messages about one entity keep their order
#   purpose       a short note for humans
# Replication is always 3 (one copy per broker) and is set by the script.
# Partition counts re-derived for NYC TLC real-scale fleet/demand (~106,000
# licensed vehicles, ~655,000 trips/day full-scale - see h-bootstrap's own
# scale settings): driver_location/rider_location carry by far the most
# messages and scale with fleet size, so they get the most headroom for
# consumer parallelism (cache-updater, clickhouse-sink) if those services
# are ever run as more than one instance. trip_requests/trip_lifecycle scale
# with request volume, which stays modest even at full scale (well under
# 1,000 messages/minute) - some headroom, not as much. city_hotspots is
# capped at 263 possible keys (one per real TLC zone) regardless of fleet
# or demand scale, so it stays at one partition per broker.
# The cdc.* topics are NOT listed here: Debezium creates them itself, one
# per PostgreSQL table (see d-infra-debezium).
# name
driver_location
column4: where each driver is, every few seconds

column1: rider_location
column4: where each rider's phone is during a trip

column1: trip_requests
column4: a passenger asks for a ride

column1: trip_lifecycle
column4: every status change of a trip, up to the final fare

column1: city_hotspots
column4: demand score per city zone, published by city-service
